item.title: Local LLM Statistics (November 2026)
item.description:
On 2026-11-22, Ollama had the most GitHub stars of the 10 local LLM projects we checked (187,830) and the most PyPI downloads (12,622,442 for its ollama package last month). These local LLM statistics were collected by aiagentmemory.org from the GitHub REST API, pypistats.org and the npm registry on 2026-11-22 at 09:21 UTC. We did not run any model ourselves.

Local runners do not keep memory. Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp process each request on its own. If you want a local model to remember past chats, see how to give a local LLM memory, Claude Code with Ollama and Codex with Ollama.

item.title: Codex with Ollama (2026): Local Models Setup and Memory
item.description: Codex with Ollama means running OpenAI’s Codex CLI against a model that Ollama serves, either on your own machine or in Ollama’s cloud. Ollama’s Codex page says you can start it with one command, ollama launch codex, or with codex --oss, which uses Ollama as the local provider. Codex still edits your files and runs your commands. The model decides how well it does that, so pick one that handles tool calls.

item.title: Claude Code with Ollama (2026): Local Models Setup and Memory
item.description: Claude Code with Ollama means running Anthropic’s coding agent against a model served by Ollama, either on your own machine or in Ollama’s cloud. Ollama’s docs say it connects Claude Code to local and cloud models through an Anthropic-compatible API, and the quickest start is one command: ollama launch claude. The model does the thinking, but Claude Code still reads your files and runs commands, so the quality of the result depends on the model you pick.

item.title: Largest Context Window Open-Source LLMs (Local, 2026)
item.description: The largest context window open-source LLM as of November 2026 is Llama 4 Scout, with 10M tokens. A wider group supports about 1M: Llama 4 Maverick, Kimi K3 and the new Kimi K3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4, GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M3, Mistral Large 4 and Meta’s Muse Spark Open. Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.8 run 262,144 tokens natively. Running any of them at full length locally is limited by GPU memory, not the model card.

item.title: How to Give a Local LLM Memory (Ollama, SQLite, Python)
item.description: A local LLM has no memory of its own. Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp process each request and keep nothing. To give a local LLM memory, use a chat app with a memory feature (Open WebUI, AnythingLLM), connect a local MCP memory server, or build it: save facts to SQLite or a local vector store, embed them with a local model, and add the relevant ones to each prompt. For a lightweight open-source agent in Python with SQLite memory on Ollama, use Agno (Apache-2.0) or the short script below. Every tool here is free to run locally, with no usage limits beyond your hardware (licenses). To run the Claude Code coding agent on a local Ollama model, see Claude Code with Ollama.
